note:
1921 Derby Road - Derby Terrace, Edgemont House and Clinton Terrace - schedules 47 to 58, read from the
householders' schedules supplied by A. Hagues on 27 September 2026.

Seven of the twelve households place themselves. In 1921 a servant's place of work is the house she
lives in, and these give it plainly: "3 Derby Terrace", "153 Derby Rd", "151 Derby Rd", "Edgmont, 143
Derby Rd" (seven servants and the manageress), "Nursing Home, 139 Derby Rd", "5 Clinton Terrace, 135
Derby Road" - which writes both of the house's numbers - and "131 Derby Rd".

Where the Derby Terrace numbers first supplied disagreed with the servants, A. Hagues confirmed the
servants: schedule 56 is 153 Derby Road and schedule 55 is 151.

Schedule 51 is a nursing home returned on the institution schedule, with a matron, a sister, a nurse,
a servant and four patients. Only its first page was supplied; the household continues at line 11.

Schedule 52 is Edgemont House, thirty-one people in fifty rooms.
source: 1921 census - Derby Terrace, Edgemont House and Clinton Terrace, schedules 43 to 58, transcribed by A. Hagues.

people.title: Sir
people.bio:
**Sir Compton Mackenzie**, novelist - in this record as the son of [[Virginia Compton]], who was boarding at Edgemont House on Derby Road in April 1921 while she ran the Grand Theatre in Nottingham. **He was not a resident of The Park himself.**

Edward Montague Compton Mackenzie was born on 17 January 1883, eldest of the five children of the actor-manager Edward Compton and Virginia Frances Bateman. He wrote novels, biography, history and a memoir that ran to ten volumes, and was as well known in his lifetime as a broadcaster and talker as for the books.

Two of his novels are still read and both were filmed: **Whisky Galore**, about a Hebridean island that helps itself to a wrecked cargo, and **The Monarch of the Glen**.

He was a Scottish nationalist all his life, and in 1928 was one of the founders of the **National Party of Scotland** with Hugh MacDiarmid, R. B. Cunninghame Graham and John MacCormick. He was appointed OBE and knighted in the Birthday Honours of 1952. He died on 30 November 1972.
